summary: The proof is correct and complete. The simplex argument establishes boundedness and equality of essential and pointwise suprema for the given globally log-concave version, including possible exceptional infinite values. The level-set identities and integrals are exact. Approximate modes justify volume scaling without an attained mode or lower semicontinuity; the Laplace-transform argument then proves the first-moment bound. Markov and Hölder yield the stated constant. Boundary cases, null level sets, unbounded support, and nonattained suprema introduce no gaps.
